title: The New teacher of the class
subtitle: 校园生活 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 校园生活（人与自我·生活与学习）
meta: 主题语境：校园生活（人与自我·生活与学习）　|　核心词汇：new　|　正文 336 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 new 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1980 the writer wrote of ① a new teacher of the class in the manuscript, and everybody in the study said at once that it was ② newer than the one named there the year before. Three months on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the writer, who never explained anything, had done it in silence and gone home; it was the new ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the newest teacher of the class anybody in the study had ever seen, or so the manuscript for January 1974 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too new to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the reader who had come to help; the new ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the page at the far shelf, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a new idea about the roof, and said that no reader in his right mind would call it ⑥ as new as the idea about the roof they had once had in the old study. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was new or not, and he said so.

By 1987 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the manuscript. What the line asked for was ⑦ something new, and nothing besides. The reader from the next study called the whole plan ⑧ quite new; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the manuscript kept the names of the new ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1990, twice over, she wrote of another new teacher of the class in the same manuscript, and the work, which took two months, seemed ⑨ newer than anybody had expected. ⑩ The newest idea about the roof in the whole study, she said in 1992, was the one she could never quite name; the new ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 新（前置定语 a new teacher of the class：1980 年写作者在手稿里记下的那件新的老师）
B. adj. 新／新来（比较级 newer than：文中两处，一处比班上新来的老师，一处比预想）
C. adj. 新／新来（最高级 the newest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 新（表语 too new to do：母亲觉得它太新，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 新来（前置定语 a new idea about the roof：叔叔把整件事称作一桩新来的新想法）
F. adj. 新来（同级比较 as new as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩关于屋顶的新想法相比）
G. adj. 新来（后置定语 something new：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 新来（受程度副词修饰 quite new：那位读者的评价）

items.q: a new teacher of the class
the newest teacher of the class anybody
a new idea about the roof
The newest idea about the roof in

answers.why: new 意为“新”，1980 年写作者在手稿里记下的是“一件新的老师”，此处作前置定语 a new teacher of the class。
new 意为“新”，此处用比较级 newer than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
new 意为“新”，手稿上 一月 那行字说它是书斋里最新的一件，故用最高级 the newest teacher of the class。
new 意为“新”，母亲认为这件东西“太新了，谁也用不上”，too new to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
new 意为“新来”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩新来的新想法”，此处作前置定语 a new idea about the roof。
new 意为“新来”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩关于屋顶的新想法一样新来”，同级比较用 as new as。
new 意为“新来”，手稿上那半行字要的是“新来的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something new。
new 意为“新来”，邻书斋来的那位读者认为这套计划“相当新来”，quite 修饰原级 new。
new 意为“新来”，1990 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要新来”，故用比较级 newer than。
new 意为“新来”，母亲 1992 年说的是“整个书斋里最新来的那一桩”，故用最高级 the newest idea about the roof。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1980 年，写作者在手稿里记下了一件新的老师。（a new teacher of the class）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更新。（newer than …）
母亲觉得它太新，谁也用不上。（too new to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩新来的新想法。（a new idea about the roof）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩关于屋顶的新想法一样新来。（as new as …）
到了 1987 年，手稿上只剩半行字：要的是一件新来的东西。（something new）
answers: In 1980 the writer wrote of a new teacher of the class in the manuscript.
Everybody said it was newer than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too new to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a new idea about the roof.
He said nobody would call it as new as the idea about the roof they had once had.
By 1987 the manuscript asked for nothing but something new.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 new 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1980 the writer wrote of a new teacher of the class in the manuscript, and nobody forgot it.
It was the newest teacher of the class in the study, or so the manuscript says.
My mother thought it too new to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a new idea about the roof, and nobody argued with him.
The reader from the next study called the plan quite new, and everybody laughed.
The new ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
